appraisal_events.evidence: « Jupien est un brave homme, la petite est charmante, il serait affreux de leur causer du chagrin. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus explicitly affirms Jupien's good character and refuses, out of genuine attachment, to let Morel target Jupien's daughter.

appraisal_events.evidence: Morel, chargé de le payer et gardant une partie de l'argent pour lui... sa nature, folle dans son genre, mais ingrate et mesquine, ne pouvait répondre que par une sécheresse ou une violence toujours croissantes
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly characterizes Morel as dishonest (skimming money via inflated mileage) and as ungrateful and petty in his response to Charlus's indulgence.

appraisal_events.evidence: Elle le regardait avec des yeux agrandis... Ils avaient l'air d'être dans un tête-à-tête mystérieux, rendu muet par ma présence... j'étais le tiers gênant et de qui on se cache.
appraisal_events.explanation: Albertine's absorbed attention toward the waiter stages the narrator, in the scene, as an excluded third party losing emotional leverage, though the passage notes this feeling was soon forgotten.

status_effects.explanation: Jupien receives a brief but clear affirmation of good character from Charlus.
Morel is explicitly characterized by the narrator as dishonest, ungrateful, and petty toward Charlus's generosity.
The narrator is staged as a marginalized third party when Albertine's attention shifts to the waiter, though the effect is described as transient.
